accepts.name: the smallest cloud, machines/cloud_links.fleet verbatim: a box between a front link and a core link, a till that asks and a core that is asked
accepts.source:
-- cloud_links.fleet -- the smallest cloud, judged as one thing: a box that is the way between
-- a front link and a core link, a client on the front, a server on the core (FWD-1, fleet v0.2).
--
-- Every check this file makes is one no single machine can fail. The box forwards, and is
-- right to; the till's route to the core is right; the core's route back is right. A box that
-- forwards between links nobody declared joined is a door nobody agreed to; a till whose route
-- has a way there and a server with none back is a street that goes one way. Each of the
-- machines is faultless alone, and the set is what is wrong. That is what a fleet is for.
--
-- LINKS names the wires these machines share: a network of one of these names, on any member,
-- is that wire. ROUTE says two of them are joined, and through whom: the member must be on both,
-- must say FORWARD, and every other member on either link must take the way -- by a gateway it
-- declares, or by a lease from the one machine that can offer it. A route is a way BOTH ways,
-- because no filter exists to make it one-way, and an answer needs a way back as much as a
-- question needs a way there (a filter is a later seat of doc/CLOUD.md).
--
-- HARDWARE says which physical unit each member is, which is what lets the court hold the
-- addresses the box PROMISES against the devices that will ask (HDW-1). The box has none: it
-- is nobody's peer, and its two NICs are the emulator's business.
--
-- experiment/os8_links.sh boots the three machines on two wires and reads their hardware
-- addresses from here.

DEFINE FLEET cloud_links AS (
  LINKS [front, core]
) RATIONALE "One front link, one core link, and a box that is both links' server and the way between"

DEFINE MEMBER gateway AS (
  DECLARATION "cloud_front.machine"
) RATIONALE "The box: it serves both links and is the way between them. It is nobody's peer, so it says no hardware"

DEFINE MEMBER till AS (
  DECLARATION "cloud_till.machine",
  HARDWARE "52:54:00:12:35:61"
) RATIONALE "The client on the front link: the device the box promises 192.168.20.40 to"

DEFINE MEMBER core AS (
  DECLARATION "cloud_core.machine",
  HARDWARE "52:54:00:12:35:62"
) RATIONALE "The machine the server is placed on, on the core link: the device the box promises 10.20.0.2 to"

DEFINE ROUTE front_to_core AS (
  BETWEEN [front, core],
  THROUGH gateway
) RATIONALE "The clients on the front link reach the servers on the core link through the box, and the servers answer them the same way: the smallest cloud has a front link, a core link, and one way between"

files.cloud_front.machine:
-- cloud_front.machine -- the box of the smallest cloud: the way between
-- its front link and its core link (FWD-1, rung 2 of the cloud ladder,
-- doc/CLOUD.md).
--
--      till ---- front link ---- [ this box ] ---- core link ---- commons
--      (asks)    192.168.20.0/24                    10.20.0.0/24   (RingServ)
--
-- It does four things, each one a declaration and none an accident:
--
--   serves both links      a DOMAIN on each makes it the link's own server of
--                          addresses and names (NAM-1). There is no pool: it
--                          admits the two peers declared below and nobody else
--   is the way             FORWARD, so a packet that arrives on one link may
--                          leave by the other, and nothing here filters it
--   offers itself          because it forwards, the lease it gives carries it as
--                          the router, and every device it serves learns the way
--   answers across links   because it is the way, it answers for the FULL names
--                          on the other link too: `commons.core.cloud` on the
--                          front link, and not the bare word `commons`, which is
--                          a name on THIS link only
--
-- It declares no EGRESS and no GATEWAY: it knows the two links it is on and no
-- way off them, and it says so by saying nothing (a machine that forwards
-- cannot say `EGRESS none`: it is a way off every link it joins).
--
-- Which links such a box may join is a fact about a SET, and a fleet declares
-- it: machines/cloud_links.fleet. experiment/os8_links.sh boots this box
-- with the till and the core on two wires, and the till reaches the thing it
-- named. The two hardware addresses below are the devices that will ask
-- (HDW-1): the fleet holds them against the members that claim them.

DEFINE MACHINE cloud_front AS (
  PROFILE hosted,
  ARCH x86_64,
  KERNEL linux,
  CONSOLE "/dev/ttyS0",
  FORWARD yes
) RATIONALE "The box of a front link and a core link: it is both links' own server of names, and the way between them"

DEFINE CAPABILITY network AS (
  GRANT yes
) RATIONALE "A machine that serves two links and is the way between them speaks on both"

DEFINE NETWORK front AS (
  INTERFACE "eth0",
  ADDRESS "192.168.20.1/24",
  DOMAIN "front.cloud"
) RATIONALE "The link the clients are on: the first address on it, answering for every name on it"

DEFINE NETWORK core AS (
  INTERFACE "eth1",
  ADDRESS "10.20.0.1/24",
  DOMAIN "core.cloud"
) RATIONALE "The link the servers are on, behind the box: nothing on it is reachable from the front link unless this machine is the way, and it is"

DEFINE PEER till AS (
  NETWORK front,
  HARDWARE "52:54:00:12:35:61",
  ADDRESS "192.168.20.40"
) RATIONALE "The till, a client: the same address every day and a name it may be found by"

DEFINE PEER commons AS (
  NETWORK core,
  HARDWARE "52:54:00:12:35:62",
  ADDRESS "10.20.0.2"
) RATIONALE "The server the solution runs on: the front link asks for it by the name commons.core.cloud and is told where it is"
files.cloud_till.machine:
-- cloud_till.machine -- the client of the smallest cloud: a device that is told
-- nothing but its own address, asks for a server by name, and goes there
-- (FWD-1, rung 2 of the cloud ladder, doc/CLOUD.md).
--
-- It declares no resolver, no gateway and no address of the server. It comes up,
-- asks the front link who it is, and is told its address, the name of the link,
-- where to ask about names, and -- because the box that answers is also the way
-- between links -- the router. Then the four questions below, in order, which
-- are the whole scene:
--
--   where    what does the name of the server on the OTHER link mean?
--   reach    ask that server a question, and say what it answered. This is the
--            line that proves a packet crossed: a name that resolves and a way
--            that is closed look the same until somebody connects
--   bare     the same word with no domain: a name on THIS link, which nobody
--            declared, so the box says there is no such name and does not guess
--   outside  a name in the rest of the world: the box speaks for its own links
--            and for the links it is the way to, and is silent about the rest
--
-- Its EGRESS is the one thing here that is a fact about ANOTHER link, written
-- in this file: the core's prefix. It is the perimeter, because a till that
-- reaches everything through a box that is the way to two links claims more
-- than the box can deliver; and it is the one place the fleet court holds
-- against the set (machines/cloud_links.fleet): a prefix no link of the fleet
-- has is a route to nowhere.

DEFINE MACHINE cloud_till AS (
  PROFILE hosted,
  ARCH x86_64,
  KERNEL linux,
  CONSOLE "/dev/ttyS0"
) RATIONALE "A client that is told everything it needs by the link it is plugged into, and declares only how far it may reach"

DEFINE CAPABILITY process AS (
  GRANT yes
) RATIONALE "The questions are processes"

DEFINE CAPABILITY network AS (
  GRANT yes
) RATIONALE "It has to ask, and then to connect"

DEFINE NETWORK front AS (
  INTERFACE "eth0",
  ADDRESS dhcp,
  EGRESS ["10.20.0.0/24"]
) RATIONALE "It asks the link. The address, the domain, the resolver and the way are the box's to give; the perimeter -- the core link and nowhere else -- is this file's to say"

DEFINE SERVICE where AS (
  RUN ["/harb", "ask", "commons.core.cloud"],
  RESTART never,
  NEEDS [process, network]
) RATIONALE "The server on the other link, asked for by its full name: the box that is the way answers for it"

DEFINE SERVICE reach AS (
  RUN ["/harb", "get", "commons.core.cloud", "8210", "/health"],
  RESTART never,
  AFTER [where],
  NEEDS [process, network]
) RATIONALE "Going there: the application's own answer to the question 'are you serving?', from a device on another link, through the box"

DEFINE SERVICE bare AS (
  RUN ["/harb", "ask", "commons"],
  RESTART never,
  AFTER [reach],
  NEEDS [process, network]
) RATIONALE "A bare word is a name on this link, and nobody declared it here: the same word on the far link is another device, and the box does not lend it"

DEFINE SERVICE outside AS (
  RUN ["/harb", "ask", "www.example.com"],
  RESTART never,
  AFTER [bare],
  NEEDS [process, network]
) RATIONALE "The rest of the world: the box speaks for its links and is silent about everything else, and does not go and ask on the till's behalf"
files.cloud_core.machine:
-- cloud_core.machine -- a member of the core link of the smallest cloud: the
-- machine a server is placed on, behind a box that is the way (FWD-1, rung 2
-- of the cloud ladder, doc/CLOUD.md).
--
-- It carries no service of its own, as machines/qemu_cloud.machine does not:
-- `harb place` puts machines/ringserv.pack on it (experiment/os8_links.sh does,
-- and boots the result). What is new here is where it stands. It asks the core
-- link for its address, and the box that serves that link has PROMISED it one
-- (the peer `commons` in machines/cloud_front.machine), so the server that
-- answers to commons.core.cloud is the one at that address and nobody else.
--
-- Its EGRESS is the way back: the front link's prefix, through the router the
-- lease carries. A server that can be asked from the front link and cannot
-- answer it is the street that goes one way, and the fleet court refuses it
-- (machines/cloud_links.fleet): reachability is a fact about two machines at
-- once, and each of them is faultless alone.
--
-- It declares its own loopback, like qemu_cloud, because the program that says
-- the server is serving asks 127.0.0.1 (SRV-2). A loopback is declared and is
-- not a link: it is no NIC and no side of a way.

DEFINE MACHINE cloud_core AS (
  PROFILE hosted,
  ARCH x86_64,
  KERNEL linux,
  CONSOLE "/dev/ttyS0"
) RATIONALE "A machine that grants what a server world asks and stands on the core link of a cloud, behind the box"

DEFINE CAPABILITY network AS (
  GRANT yes
) RATIONALE "A server world listens on the machine's network"

DEFINE CAPABILITY filesystem AS (
  GRANT yes
) RATIONALE "A server world keeps its data on a declared mount"

DEFINE CAPABILITY process AS (
  GRANT yes
) RATIONALE "The program that says a server is serving starts the server, so a world here may start a program"

DEFINE CAPABILITY threads AS (
  GRANT yes
) RATIONALE "A server world answers on several threads, and the machine sizes them with TASKS, not with this"

DEFINE CAPABILITY clock AS (
  GRANT yes
) RATIONALE "A server world timestamps what it keeps; the machine has no trusted clock and says so elsewhere (STZ-OS-RULING-07)"

DEFINE MOUNT data AS (
  AT "/data",
  FS ext4,
  DEVICE "/dev/vda",
  OPTIONS [rw, noatime]
) RATIONALE "Where a server world keeps its database: a partition that survives the power"

DEFINE NETWORK core AS (
  INTERFACE "eth0",
  ADDRESS dhcp,
  EGRESS ["192.168.20.0/24"]
) RATIONALE "It asks the core link. The box has promised it one address, and its lease carries the way to the front link: the answers to a question that came from there go back through the same box"

DEFINE NETWORK loopback AS (
  INTERFACE "lo",
  ADDRESS "127.0.0.1/8"
) RATIONALE "The machine's own loopback, so that the readiness probe can ask its own server a question; no route leaves the machine by it"
